answers.how: Measured the height of the astronaut in pixels at various times to compute the scale factor and 3D distance. Computed 3D coordinates using pixel positions and depth. The velocity at t=0.5s is the derivative of the 3D position.
Derived the acceleration by taking the second derivative of the 3D position over time, revealing a constant deceleration as the astronaut moves.
Calculated the 3D position at t=1s using the known depth and the pixel tracking, then found the instantaneous speed from the fitted trajectory.
The acceleration is constant throughout the video, calculated from the parabolic fit of the 3D coordinates.
Determined the velocity vector at t=2s from the fitted 3D kinematics, taking into account the constant acceleration opposite to the motion.
The total 3D acceleration remains constant at 0.81 m/s^2.
Used the established initial velocity and constant acceleration to compute the speed at t=3s.
Acceleration is uniform over time, derived from the consistent quadratic change in 3D position.
